Clarify that the remote connection methods share workspaces and agents on the current machine, rather than connect to agents elsewhere. Both descriptions list vscode.dev/agents; Dev Tunnels describes workspace and agent access, while GitHub Environments describes agent access across VS Code and GitHub surfaces.

Remove the extra GitHub Environments dropdown hover, retaining the preview badge and the main sharing toggle's data-handling disclosure. Update the focused tests for the new descriptions and absence of dropdown hovers.

Validation:
- `npm run build-fast -- --client-only` — passed.
- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/electron-browser/toggleRemoteConnectionsActionViewItem.test.ts --grep RemoteConnectionsActionViewItem --reporter dot` — passed, 55 tests.
- `npm run eslint -- src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/electron-browser/toggleRemoteConnectionsActionViewItem.ts src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/electron-browser/toggleRemoteConnectionsActionViewItem.test.ts` — passed.
- `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD` — passed.
- Launched the Agents window and verified both descriptions fit without truncation. Hover removal is covered by the focused tests.

CI on head `5dc4655` passed: Code OSS (compile/hygiene, Electron, browser, remote, and smoke tests across Linux, macOS, and Windows), Component Fixtures, CodeQL, Monaco Editor checks, and Telemetry. Copilot review completed with no findings.

Scenarios.Scenario: Opening the Remote Connections method picker from the chat input toolbar
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A mouse/keyboard open synchronously calls the two-item action provider, reads the local backend configuration, localizes two constant strings, builds the action-list items, and renders the popup before it becomes usable.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Exactly two connection-method rows per open. The PR lengthens two fixed detail strings but does not increase row cardinality or introduce input-dependent work.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Entirely synchronous UI work; there are no promises, queues, IPC calls, subprocesses, filesystem operations, database operations, or network requests on the changed menu-construction path.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache participates; the same two actions are rebuilt on every open both before and after the PR. Cold and repeated opens differ only in existing framework rendering state, not in changed work.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in the call path and fixed cardinality from RemoteConnectionsActionViewItem._getConnectionMethods through ActionWidgetDropdown.show and ActionWidgetService.show.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact text-layout cost varies with font, localization, and popup width, but remains bounded to two rows and does not establish a user-visible regression.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The only added work is rendering longer constant text for two rows; it neither adds a scaling mechanism nor crosses an expensive boundary.

Scenarios.Scenario: Focusing or hovering the GitHub Environments picker row
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The already-rendered action-list row handles focus or pointer movement. The changed action no longer supplies flyout-hover content, so the action list has no extra hover to construct or display for this row.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One fixed row per user focus/hover event; the PR removes its optional hover metadata rather than adding per-event or retained work.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous pointer/focus handling only, with no asynchronous work or boundary calls introduced by the diff.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No relevant cache or coalescing exists. Before the PR the row carried hover content on every menu open; afterward it does not, for both cold and repeated interactions.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence because the changed field maps directly to IActionListItem.hover in ActionWidgetDropdown.show, and the diff deletes that field.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The amount of UI work saved by omitting the flyout is small and interaction-dependent, but there is no plausible degradation mechanism.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The change removes optional hover UI work and retained metadata rather than adding performance cost.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over the full two-file diff and traced the menu-open and row-hover paths. The PR changes two bounded strings and removes one hover configuration; it adds no expensive boundary, concurrency, cache-lifecycle, repeated-work, or unbounded-retention mechanism, so no findings were submitted.
